name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the very top of every page that jumps directly to the main content. This fixes keyboard navigation for users who rely on screen readers or tabbing, bypassing repetitive navigation blocks. The trade-off is one extra DOM element, but it’s negligible compared to the usability gain for millions who navigate without a mouse.

name: Reader
text: Risk: A single skip link fails when pages have *three* or more distinct navigation blocks (e.g., header, sidebar, footer). Better alternative: Add a *set* of skip links—one per major region—so users can jump directly to the region they need. Settle it by testing with screen-reader users on a page with multiple nav blocks; if they still can’t reach content, the set wins.

name: Ramp
text:
We should add a set of skip links, one per major region, to allow users to jump directly to the section they need. This approach is better than a single skip link because it provides more flexibility and convenience for users with multiple navigation blocks. The trade-off is a slightly more complex implementation and a minimal increase in cognitive load for users who must choose which skip link to use. By doing this, we ensure that users who rely on screen readers or keyboard navigation can efficiently access the content they need, which is a top priority for making EXCAVA usable by everyone.

name: Reader
text: Risk: A set of skip links risks cluttering the page for *all* users—especially on mobile or reduced-motion settings—if not hidden by default and keyboard-triggered. Better alternative: A single skip link that cycles through regions (e.g., header → main → footer) via repeated activation. Settle it by testing with screen-reader users on a page with three+ navigation blocks.
